answer.rationale: Competitive price pressure on SMB base requires immediate, targeted response. memory_73 confirms promotional pricing drives acquisition and revenue lift in price-sensitive SMB segments. memory_57 shows referral incentives work but are concentrated in established (6+ month) accounts—insufficient for immediate churn defense. memory_86 and memory_31 show onboarding/activation improvements drive adoption, but these are medium-term plays; activation_messaging (memory_91) similarly targets engagement rather than price elasticity. enterprise_sales_assist (exp_44) is orthogonal to SMB churn. Promotional pricing is the only lever that directly addresses price sensitivity driving current churn. Standard experiment scale allows controlled rollout to price-sensitive SMB cohorts with monitoring for margin degradation and retention cliff risk. Flagged downstream risk: aggressive promotional pricing may anchor customer expectations, increase churn elasticity post-promotion, or erode margin sustainability. Preserves uncertainty by running as time-limited experiment rather than permanent structural change, allowing measurement of retention and LTV impact before broad commitment.
